## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Mahākassapa Sutta* (Ud 1.6) is the sixth discourse of the first chapter (Bodhivagga) of the *Udāna* [Holt et al. 2003]. The discourse recounts how the Venerable Mahākassapa, having just recovered from an extended illness, sets out on an alms-seeking round [Holt et al. 2003]. Although various deities (*deva*s) attempt to present him with food offerings, Mahākassapa turns down their gifts and deliberately chooses to seek alms among the poor and destitute instead [SuttaCentral; Holt et al. 2003]. In modern scholarship, this narrative has been analyzed alongside a closely related alms expedition later in the collection (Ud 3.7, *Sakkudāna Sutta*), drawing an analogy between emerging from prolonged illness and emerging from a seven-day meditative absorption (*samādhi*) [Holt et al. 2003]. The narrative background is further developed in Dhammapāla's *Udāna-aṭṭhakathā* [Holt et al. 2003].
SuttaCentral identifies passage-level parallels to this discourse in two versions of the *Udānavarga* (UV 33, *Brāhmaṇavarga*; Uv Kg 33) and in the *Paṭhamagilānasutta* (SN 46.14), which likewise concerns Mahākassapa's illness; the text is also cited in the *Cūḷaniddesa* (Cnd 23) [SuttaCentral]. In canonical and paracanonical text reuse, DharmaNexus detects 74 matching passages across 15 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its strongest internal relationship is with Ud 3.7 (§0.2–2.3 ↔ §0.2–2.3), matching 1,359 characters with an 0.86 similarity score, confirming the close structural affinity between the two alms stories [DharmaNexus; Holt et al. 2003]. Substantial parallels and reuse also occur in the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* and *Udāna-aṭṭhakathā*, as well as formulaic shared passages across the *Khandha Saṁyutta* (SN 22), *Bojjhaṅga Saṁyutta* (SN 46), *Chakkanipāta* (AN 6), *Satipaṭṭhāna Saṁyutta* (SN 47), and the Vinaya Khandhaka treatises [DharmaNexus].
